data.title: Europe's Aviation Authorities Struggle to Contain Wave of Bomb Threats
data.description: According to CNBC, more than two dozen bomb threats against passenger flights across Europe this week have prompted diversions, emergency landings and military escorts. Authorities have described the threats as malicious hoaxes, and no attacks have occurred. A threat naming a specific flight already in the air triggers international procedures requiring a prompt landing, evacuation and searches, aviation security consultant Wilfried Covent said. National authorities handle threat assessments and security measures in coordination with airlines, airports and law enforcement. A single diversion can cost an airline as much as $250,000, including expenses for replacement crews, missed connections and disruption to the day's schedule, aviation security professor Philip Baum told AP.

data.title: Microsoft Spends $5 Billion Less on Data Centers as Supermicro Raises Revenue Outlook
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing The Information and Bernstein, Microsoft’s third-quarter capital spending was about $5 billion below plan after third-party data centers it intended to lease were delayed. An Iren project in Childress, Texas, was among the causes, deferring some of Microsoft’s spending. Microsoft had announced plans to spend $9.7 billion over five years to lease servers equipped with Nvidia GPUs from Iren.

Microsoft also withdrew last month from a planned data center lease with Nscale in the UK over delays in grid access. With its own data center construction unable to meet demand quickly, Microsoft is renting computing capacity from multiple cloud providers. Supermicro reported first-quarter revenue of $19.95 billion, above analysts’ expectations of $16.39 billion, and forecast second-quarter revenue of $19.5 billion to $21.5 billion. It raised its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to $72 billion to $82 billion, from $65 billion to $72 billion. Bernstein said AI computing demand assessments should account for contract cancellation terms, duration and deployment timing, since projects may be delivered in phases and chip procurement and data center lease agreements may cover the same capacity.

data.title: ByteDance Considers Expanding Brazil Data Center Project
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, TikTok parent ByteDance is considering expanding its data center project at the Pecém Industrial and Port Complex in Ceará, northeastern Brazil, and is seeking a developer for the second phase. The phase could be larger than the facility currently under construction in the state, which involves a $10 billion investment and 300 megawatts of capacity, according to people familiar with the matter.

ByteDance has also held preliminary talks with developers about a similarly sized data center outside the port to serve Brazilian customers. Data centers inside the port must export data to qualify for tax incentives. ByteDance previously announced plans to invest 200 billion reais, or about $36 billion, in the complex in phases. Construction on the first phase began in early 2026.

data.title: Keplr Suspends Google and Apple Logins After Unauthorized Transactions Reported
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, crypto wallet Keplr has suspended Google and Apple social login after users reported unauthorized transactions on their accounts. Keplr said in an initial assessment that accounts restored with a seed phrase or using a hardware wallet were unaffected. It advised users who created accounts through social login to stop transferring funds into them.

data.description: Hyperliquid said on Discord that it will upgrade its network around 4:15 PM on November 7. According to Foresight News, services are expected to be paused for about 10 minutes.

data.title: Bitdeer Sells 258.6 BTC This Week, Maintains Zero Bitcoin Holdings
data.description: Bitdeer sold 258.6 BTC this week and maintained zero bitcoin holdings. According to Odaily, the company’s weekly update said it produced 258.6 BTC as of November 6, sold all of it, and had no net additions; its holdings remained at zero, excluding customer deposits.

data.title: Cyber Repurchased Approximately $13 Million Worth of CYBER Tokens Over the Past Year
data.description: Cyber, a social data protocol, said it repurchased approximately $13 million worth of CYBER tokens over the past year. According to Foresight News, the protocol said it would continue supporting the growth and development of its ecosystem.

data.title: Glassnode: Bitcoin-S&P 500 Correlation Reaches 0.8, Highest Since 2020
data.description: Glassnode reported that Bitcoin's correlation with the S&P 500 reached 0.8 over the past 30 U.S. trading sessions, its highest level since 2020. According to PANews, which reported the update on November 7, the correlation was well below 0.8 for most of the period since 2020. The post added that although Bitcoin's relative strength is sometimes discussed, macro factors continue to determine the broader market direction.

data.description: Dash urged users not to use Eclipse, saying some users lost funds while attempting trades and have not been fully compensated. According to Odaily, Dash recommended platforms such as Maya Protocol and NEAR Intents, where swap processes can be viewed through block explorers.

data.title: Najib Razak’s Move to House Arrest Delayed for Royal Pardon Review
data.description: Former Malaysian Prime Minister Najib Razak’s transfer from prison to house arrest was postponed pending further review of conditions surrounding a royal pardon, the attorney general’s office said, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Crédit Agricole: Weak Economy Weighs on Canadian Dollar; Jobs Data May Set Next Direction
data.description: According to Jin10, a Crédit Agricole research report said the U.S. dollar against the Canadian dollar stabilized near 1.40 over the past week. The Democrats’ decisive victory in the U.S. midterm elections did not noticeably lift the Canadian dollar, and positive signs of renewed U.S.-Canada trade talks also failed to change the picture. Canada’s preliminary third-quarter GDP data showed growth slowing to 1.3%, below the Bank of Canada’s 2% expectation, with economic weakness continuing to weigh on the currency. The bank said attention had shifted to October’s employment report. Earlier weak employment data had raised concerns that Canada’s labor market would struggle to withstand U.S.-Canada trade tensions. Signs of a labor-market recovery could support the Canadian dollar. However, a decisive break by the U.S. dollar-Canadian dollar pair below the 200-day moving average near 1.39 would require a stronger positive catalyst.

data.title: Hong Kong SFC Plans to Restrict Unauthorized Use of “Crypto” and “Exchange” Terms
data.description: Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission has issued consultation conclusions proposing amendments to two ordinances to restrict unauthorized entities from using certain terms that could lead the public to believe they are regulated by the SFC or affiliated with an exchange, clearing house, or virtual asset trading platform. According to Odaily, the proposed restrictions cover terms such as “crypto” and “exchange.”

data.title: Goldman Sachs Raises U.S. Data Center Construction Forecast to $125 Billion in 2028
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing Goldman Sachs, the bank raised its U.S. data center construction spending forecast to $80 billion in 2026, up from $67 billion, and $100 billion in 2027, up from $87 billion. It also issued a first estimate of $125 billion for 2028. The revisions come amid market concerns over tighter data center regulation following Democrats’ win of control of Congress.

Goldman Sachs said about 86 gigawatts of data center projects are under construction in the U.S., with another roughly $900 billion in high-confidence projects awaiting construction. It said the buildout remains resilient, with demand and backlogs at hyperscalers including Microsoft, Amazon and Google showing no clear slowdown. H100 rental prices rose 26% year over year, while GB200 rental prices are up 50% year to date.

On Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa’s proposed pause on data centers, Goldman Sachs said it could delay project delivery rather than directly cancel plans, while potentially raising financing costs, reducing tax incentives and prompting some customers to cancel contracts. The bank cautioned that industry-wide growth prospects should be distinguished from individual developers’ ability to survive. Highly leveraged developers could face severe financial pressure from delays and higher financing costs, and some may not last until their projects begin operations.

data.title: BMO Capital Markets: Canadian Fiscal and Monetary Policies May Be Pulling in Opposite Directions
data.description: According to Jin10, BMO Capital Markets Chief Economist Douglas Porter said in a report published over the weekend that Canada's fiscal and monetary policies may be working in opposite directions. Porter said the Canadian government's annual budget plan was more substantial than expected and provided significant fiscal stimulus. BMO Capital Markets raised its forecast for Canada's 2027 GDP growth from 1.8% to 2%. Meanwhile, the Bank of Canada raised interest rates in response to higher inflation expectations and could raise them further. Porter said, “If that does not count as policies moving in contradictory directions, it is hard to imagine what would.” He added that weak employment data, falling oil prices and a selloff in technology stocks could prompt Bank of Canada policymakers to reassess whether another rate hike in December is necessary.

data.title: U.S. ZEC Spot ETFs Record $1.77 Million in Daily Net Inflows

data.title: PRECIOUS METALS | China’s Gold-Buying Streak Reaches Two Years as Prices Fall
data.description: China’s central bank added to its gold reserves in October, extending its buying streak to two years, as the metal fell almost 7% and ended the month below the $4,000-an-ounce support threshold, according to Bloomberg.
